grammarTopics.title: Topic Marker 'Ang' vs. 'Si'
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'ang' before common nouns and 'si' before singular personal names to mark the topic/focus.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kumakain ang bata. / Kumakain si Juan.
grammarTopics.english: The child is eating. / Juan is eating.

grammarTopics.title: Plural Markers 'Ang mga' vs. 'Sina'
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'ang mga' (pronounced 'mang-ah') for plural common nouns and 'sina' before a group of named people.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nandito na ang mga bisita. / Umalis na sina Maria at Ana.
grammarTopics.english: The guests are here already. / Maria and Ana already left.

grammarTopics.title: Actor/Possessive Marker 'Ng' vs. 'Ni'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Ng' (pronounced 'nang') marks non-focus actors, direct objects, or possession for common nouns; 'ni' does the same for personal names.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kinain ng aso ang tinapay. / Bahay ni Pedro ito.
grammarTopics.english: The dog ate the bread. / This is Pedro's house.

grammarTopics.title: Plural Actor/Possessive 'Ng mga' vs. 'Nina'
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'ng mga' for plural common nouns and 'nina' for multiple personal names.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Binili nina Carlo at Leo ang saging.
grammarTopics.english: Carlo and Leo bought the bananas.

grammarTopics.title: Locative/Directional Marker 'Sa' vs. 'Kay'
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'sa' for places, directions, and time, and 'kay' when directing an action to a specific person.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Pupunta ako sa palengke. / Ibigay mo ito kay Nanay.
grammarTopics.english: I am going to the wet market. / Give this to Mom.

grammarTopics.title: Plural Directional 'Sa mga' vs. 'Kina'
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'kina' before a person's name to mean 'at/to [Person]'s place' or 'to [Person and companions]'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Makikitulog muna ako kina Tita.
grammarTopics.english: I'll sleep over at Auntie's house for now.

grammarTopics.title: Ang-Pronouns (Ako, Ikaw/Ka, Siya)
grammarTopics.explanation: Singular topic pronouns. 'Ikaw' is used at the start of a sentence or standalone; 'ka' is an enclitic placed after the first word.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ikaw ba ang bago? / Kumain ka na ba?
grammarTopics.english: Are you the new one? / Have you eaten already?

grammarTopics.title: Plural Ang-Pronouns (Tayo, Kami, Kayo, Sila)
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Tayo' includes the listener (inclusive 'we'); 'kami' excludes the listener (exclusive 'we').
grammarTopics.tagalog: Tara, kain na tayo! / Aalis na kami, ingat kayo.
grammarTopics.english: Come on, let's eat! / We (not you) are leaving now, take care (you all).

grammarTopics.title: Ng-Pronouns (Ko, Mo, Niya)
grammarTopics.explanation: Used for possession after a noun or as the actor of object-focus verbs.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nasaan ang susi ko? / Binili niya ang kape.
grammarTopics.english: Where is my key? / He/She bought the coffee.

grammarTopics.title: Plural Ng-Pronouns (Natin, Namin, Ninyo, Nila)
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Natin' is inclusive (our/by us); 'namin' is exclusive (our/by us, excluding listener).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Bayan natin ito. / Ito ang bahay namin.
grammarTopics.english: This is our (all of us) country. / This is our (my family's) house.

grammarTopics.title: Sa-Pronouns (Akin, Iyo, Kanya)
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses strong possession before a noun (with linker) or direction toward a person.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Sa akin ang bag na ito. / Ibinigay ko sa kanya.
grammarTopics.english: This bag is mine. / I gave it to him/her.

grammarTopics.title: Dual Pronoun 'Kita'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Kita' replaces 'ko ikaw' when 'I' act upon 'you' (singular).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Mahal kita. / Tutulungan kita mamaya.
grammarTopics.english: I love you. / I will help you later.

grammarTopics.title: Demonstrative Pronouns (Ito, Iyan, Iyon)
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Ito' (this, near speaker), 'iyan' (that, near listener), 'iyon' (that over there, far from both).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Magkano ito? / Paki-abot nga iyan.
grammarTopics.english: How much is this? / Please pass that (near you).

grammarTopics.title: Locative Demonstratives (Dito, Diyan, Doon)
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Dito' (here), 'diyan' (there near you), 'doon' (over there). Often shifts to rito/riyan/roon after vowels.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Para po dito sa tabi! / Doon tayo sa kabilang kanto.
grammarTopics.english: Pull over right here on the side! / Let's go over there to the next corner.

grammarTopics.title: Ng-Demonstratives (Nito, Niyan, Noon)
grammarTopics.explanation: Marks non-focus objects or possession for demonstratives ('of this', 'of that').
grammarTopics.tagalog: Pabili po ng tatlo nito.
grammarTopics.english: I'd like to buy three of this, please.

grammarTopics.title: Polite Second-Person 'Kayo' / 'Ninyo'
grammarTopics.explanation: Using plural pronouns 'kayo' or 'ninyo' with 'po' shows deep respect to an older stranger.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Saan po kayo bababa, Manong?
grammarTopics.english: Where will you be getting off, Sir?

grammarTopics.title: Linker '-ng' vs. 'Na'
grammarTopics.explanation: Connects adjectives, numbers, or demonstratives to nouns. Use '-ng' after vowels/n, and 'na' after consonants.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Mainit na pandesal / Malamig na tubig / Dalawang kape
grammarTopics.english: Hot pandesal / Cold water / Two coffees

grammarTopics.title: Existential 'May' vs. 'Mayroon'
grammarTopics.explanation: Both mean 'there is/have'. 'May' goes directly before a noun/verb; 'mayroon' (often 'meron') can stand alone or precede enclitics.
grammarTopics.tagalog: May barya ka ba? — Oo, meron.
grammarTopics.english: Do you have loose change? — Yes, I do.

grammarTopics.title: Negative Existential 'Wala'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'none', 'nothing', or 'not present'. Takes the linker '-ng' before nouns.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Walang pasok bukas! / Wala akong dalang payong.
grammarTopics.english: There are no classes tomorrow! / I don't have an umbrella with me.

grammarTopics.title: Identification Negator 'Hindi'
grammarTopics.explanation: Negates verbs, adjectives, and nouns (unlike 'wala' which negates existence/possession).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Hindi ako marunong lumangoy. / Hindi ito akin.
grammarTopics.english: I don't know how to swim. / This is not mine.

grammarTopics.title: Actor Focus '-um-' (Infinitive / Command)
grammarTopics.explanation: Infix '-um-' is inserted before the first vowel of the root word for basic or natural actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kain -> Kumain ka na. / Upo -> Umupo muna kayo.
grammarTopics.english: Eat -> Eat now. / Sit -> Please sit down first.

grammarTopics.title: '-um-' Completed Aspect (Past)
grammarTopics.explanation: For '-um-' verbs, the completed (past) form is identical to the infinitive form.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Uminom ako ng taho kaninang umaga.
grammarTopics.english: I drank taho earlier this morning.

grammarTopics.title: '-um-' Contemplated Aspect (Future)
grammarTopics.explanation: Drop '-um-' and reduplicate the first syllable of the root word.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Bili -> Bibili ako ng ulam mamaya.
grammarTopics.english: Buy -> I will buy viand later.

grammarTopics.title: '-um-' Incompleted Aspect (Progressive)
grammarTopics.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root and insert '-um-' before the first vowel.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ulan -> Umuulan na naman sa labas!
grammarTopics.english: Rain -> It is raining outside again!

grammarTopics.title: Actor Focus 'Mag-' (Infinitive / Command)
grammarTopics.explanation: Prefix 'mag-' is used for deliberate, outward, or transitive actor-focus actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Magluto tayo ng adobo. / Mag-ingat ka sa biyahe.
grammarTopics.english: Let's cook adobo. / Take care on your trip.

grammarTopics.title: 'Mag-' Completed Aspect ('Nag-')
grammarTopics.explanation: Change the 'm-' in 'mag-' to 'n-' ('nag-') for completed past actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nagbayad na ako sa GCash.
grammarTopics.english: I already paid via GCash.

grammarTopics.title: 'Mag-' Incompleted Aspect ('Nag-' + Reduplication)
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'nag-' plus the repeated first syllable of the root for ongoing actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Naglalaba si Nanay sa likod-bahay.
grammarTopics.english: Mom is doing laundry in the backyard.

grammarTopics.title: 'Mag-' Contemplated Aspect ('Mag-' + Reduplication)
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'mag-' plus the repeated first syllable of the root for future actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Magpapahinga muna ako pag-uwi.
grammarTopics.english: I will rest first when I get home.

grammarTopics.title: Actor Focus 'Ma-' (Involuntary / State Verbs)
grammarTopics.explanation: Used for actions that happen naturally or involve bodily states (tulog, ligo, kinig).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Matulog ka na, maaga pa tayo bukas.
grammarTopics.english: Go to sleep now, we have an early start tomorrow.

grammarTopics.title: 'Ma-' Completed ('Na-') & Progressive ('Na-' + Redup)
grammarTopics.explanation: Change 'ma-' to 'na-' for past, and reduplicate the root's first syllable for progressive.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nakatulog ako sa jeep! / Natutulog pa si bunso.
grammarTopics.english: I fell asleep on the jeepney! / The youngest is still sleeping.

grammarTopics.title: Actor Focus 'Mang-' (Habitual / Plural Objects)
grammarTopics.explanation: Often triggers nasal assimilation (m/n/ng) on the root's initial consonant (bili -> mamili).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Mamamalengke kami bukas ng umaga.
grammarTopics.english: We will go marketing tomorrow morning.

grammarTopics.title: Ability / Accidental Actor Focus 'Maka-' / 'Naka-'
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses 'able to' or 'happened to' do something.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nakabili ka ba ng ticket? / Hindi ako makatulog.
grammarTopics.english: Were you able to buy a ticket? / I can't sleep.

grammarTopics.title: Stative Prefix 'Naka-' (Wearing / Posture)
grammarTopics.explanation: Describes what someone is wearing or their current physical state/position.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Naka-uniform na ako. / Nakaupo siya sa harap.
grammarTopics.english: I am already in uniform. / He/She is sitting in front.

grammarTopics.title: Recent Past Prefix 'Ka-' + Reduplication
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses an action that 'just happened' moments ago. Actor takes 'ng' or 'ko/mo'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kakakain ko lang. / Kadarating lang ng Grab.
grammarTopics.english: I just ate. / The Grab car just arrived.

grammarTopics.title: Social / Participatory Prefix 'Maki-' / 'Naki-'
grammarTopics.explanation: Used to politely ask to join in or use something belonging to others.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Makikiraan po. / Makikisuyo po ng bayad.
grammarTopics.english: Excuse me (passing through). / Please pass my fare.

grammarTopics.title: Reciprocal Prefix 'Mag- -an'
grammarTopics.explanation: Shows two or more actors doing an action to or with each other.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nagkuwentuhan kami habang nagkakape.
grammarTopics.english: We chatted with each other while having coffee.

grammarTopics.title: Pseudo-Verbs 'Gusto' and 'Ayaw'
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses 'want/like' and 'don't want/dislike'. The actor takes 'ng/ko/mo' and the object takes 'ang/ng'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Gusto ko ng halo-halo. / Ayaw niya ng maanghang.
grammarTopics.english: I want halo-halo. / He/She doesn't like spicy food.

grammarTopics.title: Pseudo-Verb 'Kailangan' (Need)
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses necessity. Followed by a linker when paired with another verb.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kailangan kong mag-load bago umalis.
grammarTopics.english: I need to buy mobile load before leaving.

grammarTopics.title: Pseudo-Verbs 'Pwede' and 'Bawal'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Pwede' means allowed/possible; 'bawal' means prohibited/forbidden.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Pwede bang mag-GCash dito? / Bawal mag-park dito.
grammarTopics.english: Is GCash accepted here? / Parking is prohibited here.

grammarTopics.title: Pseudo-Verb 'Dapat' (Should / Must)
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses obligation or what ought to be done.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Dapat magdala ka ng payong kasi maulap.
grammarTopics.english: You should bring an umbrella because it's cloudy.

grammarTopics.title: Object Focus '-in' (Infinitive / Command)
grammarTopics.explanation: Suffix '-in' (or '-hin' after vowels) puts the spotlight on the specific object being acted upon.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kainin mo na ang pansit. / Lutuin natin ito.
grammarTopics.english: Eat the pancit now. / Let's cook this.

grammarTopics.title: '-in' Completed Aspect (Infix '-in-')
grammarTopics.explanation: Drop the suffix '-in' and insert '-in-' before the first vowel of the root (or 'ni-' before l/r/w/y).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kinain ng pusa ang isda. / Niluto ni Ate ang sinigang.
grammarTopics.english: The cat ate the fish. / Older sister cooked the sinigang.

grammarTopics.title: '-in' Incompleted Aspect ('-in-' + Redup)
grammarTopics.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable and insert '-in-' for ongoing object-focused actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Binabasa ko pa ang message niya.
grammarTopics.english: I am still reading his/her message.

grammarTopics.title: '-in' Contemplated Aspect (Redup + '-in')
grammarTopics.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root and keep the '-in' suffix for future actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Bibilhin ko ang sapatos sa payday.
grammarTopics.english: I will buy the shoes on payday.

grammarTopics.title: Locative / Directional Focus '-an'
grammarTopics.explanation: Suffix '-an' (or '-han') focuses on the location, surface, or recipient of an action.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Buksan mo ang pinto. / Hugasan mo ang mga plato.
grammarTopics.english: Open the door. / Wash the plates.

grammarTopics.title: '-an' Completed Aspect ('-in- ... -an')
grammarTopics.explanation: Combine infix '-in-' with suffix '-an' for completed locative/recipient actions.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Binigyan ako ni Lola ng aguinaldo.
grammarTopics.english: Grandma gave me a Christmas gift.

grammarTopics.title: '-an' Progressive & Future Aspects
grammarTopics.explanation: Add syllable reduplication to '-in- ... -an' for progressive, and reduplication + '-an' for future.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Dinadagdagan ni Manong ang sago. / Dadalhan kita ng pagkain.
grammarTopics.english: Manong is adding more sago. / I will bring food to you.

grammarTopics.title: Benefactive / Instrumental Focus 'I-'
grammarTopics.explanation: Prefix 'i-' focuses on an item moved away from the actor, an instrument, or something done for someone.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Isara mo ang bintana. / Iabot mo nga ang asin.
grammarTopics.english: Close the window. / Please pass the salt.

grammarTopics.title: 'I-' Completed Aspect ('I- + -in-')
grammarTopics.explanation: Insert '-in-' into the root while keeping the 'i-' prefix.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ibinigay ko na ang bayad sa driver.
grammarTopics.english: I already gave the fare to the driver.

grammarTopics.title: 'I-' Progressive & Future Aspects
grammarTopics.explanation: Reduplicate the root's first syllable with 'i- + -in-' for progressive, or 'i-' + reduplication for future.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ipinapasa ko na ang file. / Iluluto ko ito mamaya.
grammarTopics.english: I am submitting the file now. / I will cook this later.

grammarTopics.title: Ability / Accidental Object Focus 'Ma-' / 'Na-'
grammarTopics.explanation: Used when the object is specific and the actor accidentally or successfully acts on it.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Naiwan ko ang payong ko sa tricycle!
grammarTopics.english: I accidentally left my umbrella in the tricycle!

grammarTopics.title: Ability / Accidental Locative Focus 'Ma- -an' / 'Na- -an'
grammarTopics.explanation: Focuses on a person or place affected accidentally or successfully.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Naabutan kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.
grammarTopics.english: We got caught in heavy rain on the road.

grammarTopics.title: Causative Prefix 'Pa-' (Having Someone Do Something)
grammarTopics.explanation: Prefix 'pa-' expresses requesting, ordering, or letting someone perform an action.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Pa-print po nito. / Nagpagupit ako sa barbero.
grammarTopics.english: Please print this. / I got a haircut at the barber.

grammarTopics.title: Polite Request Prefix 'Paki-'
grammarTopics.explanation: Attaches to verb roots to mean 'please do [verb] for me'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Paki-check naman kung pumasok na ang GCash.
grammarTopics.english: Please check if the GCash transfer went through.

grammarTopics.title: Benefactive 'Ipag-' (Doing for Someone)
grammarTopics.explanation: Focuses on the person who benefits from an action.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ipagluluto kita ng sinigang bukas.
grammarTopics.english: I will cook sinigang for you tomorrow.

grammarTopics.title: Instrumental 'Ipang-' (Using a Tool)
grammarTopics.explanation: Focuses on the tool or money used to accomplish something.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ipambili mo na lang ito ng merienda.
grammarTopics.english: Use this (money) to buy snacks.

grammarTopics.title: Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus
grammarTopics.explanation: Use Actor Focus ('ng' object) for indefinite/general objects; use Object Focus ('ang' object) for specific/definite objects.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Bumili ako ng kape. (a coffee) vs. Binili ko ang kape. (the specific coffee)
grammarTopics.english: I bought some coffee. vs. I bought the coffee.

grammarTopics.title: Imperative Softening with 'Nga'
grammarTopics.explanation: Commands in Tagalog often sound abrupt without 'nga' or 'po'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Umupo ka nga muna. / Paki-abot nga po.
grammarTopics.english: Please have a seat first. / Please pass that over.

grammarTopics.title: Negative Commands with 'Huwag' (Wag)
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'huwag' (colloquial 'wag') + infinitive verb to say 'Don't...'. Enclitics move before the verb!
grammarTopics.tagalog: Huwag kang mag-alala. / Wag mo nang bilhin iyan.
grammarTopics.english: Don't worry. / Don't buy that anymore.

grammarTopics.title: Hortative 'Tara' and 'Tayo Na'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Tara' (let's go) and 'tayo na' (let's go now) invite the listener to move together.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo sa EDSA!
grammarTopics.english: Let's go now, or we might get stuck in EDSA traffic!

grammarTopics.title: Respect Particle 'Po' and 'Opo'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Po' is inserted into sentences to show respect to elders or strangers; 'opo' means 'yes (with respect)'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Salamat po! / Opo, nandito na po ako sa gate.
grammarTopics.english: Thank you! / Yes, I am already here at the gate.

grammarTopics.title: Informal Respect 'Ho' and 'Oho'
grammarTopics.explanation: Slightly softer/less formal than 'po', commonly used in Southern Tagalog or with familiar elders.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Tuloy po kayo! / Oho, Tita, kakain na ho.
grammarTopics.english: Please come in! / Yes, Auntie, I'm about to eat.

grammarTopics.title: Change-of-State Particle 'Na'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'already' or 'now', indicating a new state or completed transition.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kumain na ako. / Tara na, umuulan na!
grammarTopics.english: I have already eaten. / Let's go now, it's raining!

grammarTopics.title: Continuation Particle 'Pa'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'still' or 'yet' (with negatives) or 'more/else'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Wala pa ang rider. / May kape pa ba?
grammarTopics.english: The rider isn't here yet. / Is there still more coffee?

grammarTopics.title: Question Particle 'Ba'
grammarTopics.explanation: Turns a statement into a yes/no question. Placed after the first word or monosyllabic pronoun.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Tapos ka na ba? / Malamig ba sa Baguio?
grammarTopics.english: Are you finished already? / Is it cold in Baguio?

grammarTopics.title: Limiting Particle 'Lang' (Lamang)
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'only', 'just', or softens a request to make it feel small and easy.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Sandali lang po. / Dito lang sa tabi.
grammarTopics.english: Just a moment, please. / Right here on the side only.

grammarTopics.title: Confirmation / Emphasis Particle 'Nga'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'indeed', 'really', or politely softens a request.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Oo nga! / Patingin nga niyan.
grammarTopics.english: Yes, indeed! / Let me take a look at that.

grammarTopics.title: Contrast / Softening Particle 'Naman'
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses gentle contrast ('on the other hand', 'this time') or polite appeal.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ikaw naman ang kumanta! / Ang init naman ngayon.
grammarTopics.english: Your turn to sing! / It's so hot today (complaining gently).

grammarTopics.title: Realization Particle 'Pala'
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or remembering something ('oh, so...').
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ikaw pala iyan! / Ay, walang pasok pala ngayon.
grammarTopics.english: Oh, it's you! / Oh, there's no class today after all.

grammarTopics.title: Sequence / Priority Particle 'Muna'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'first', 'for now', or 'before doing anything else'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kain muna tayo bago mag-aral.
grammarTopics.english: Let's eat first before studying.

grammarTopics.title: Addition Particle 'Din' / 'Rin'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'also' or 'too'. Use 'rin' after vowels/w/y and 'din' after consonants.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ako rin! / Masarap din ang bibingka nila.
grammarTopics.english: Me too! / Their bibingka is delicious as well.

grammarTopics.title: Uncertainty Particle 'Kaya'
grammarTopics.explanation: Expresses wondering or speculation ('I wonder if...', 'perhaps').
grammarTopics.tagalog: Bukas kaya ang bangko ngayon?
grammarTopics.english: I wonder if the bank is open today?

grammarTopics.title: Reported Speech Particle 'Daw' / 'Raw'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'according to someone' or 'they said'. 'Raw' follows vowels; 'daw' follows consonants.
grammarTopics.tagalog: May bagyo raw bukas. / Umalis na daw siya.
grammarTopics.english: They say there's a typhoon tomorrow. / Someone said he/she already left.

grammarTopics.title: Reason / Explanation Particle 'Kasi'
grammarTopics.explanation: Means 'because' (colloquial). Often placed right after the first word of the clause.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Late ako kasi na-traffic sa Ortigas.
grammarTopics.english: I'm late because I got stuck in Ortigas traffic.

grammarTopics.title: Golden Rule of Enclitic Ordering
grammarTopics.explanation: Monosyllabic pronouns (ka, ko, mo) come first, followed by 'na/pa', then 'ba', 'din/rin', 'lang', 'naman', 'po'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Naibigay mo na ba po?
grammarTopics.english: Have you given it already, Sir/Ma'am?

grammarTopics.title: 'Ma-' Adjectives (Descriptive Quality)
grammarTopics.explanation: Prefix 'ma-' + root forms common adjectives (masarap = delicious, mainit = hot).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Masarap ang sinigang ni Lola.
grammarTopics.english: Grandma's sinigang is delicious.

grammarTopics.title: Pluralizing 'Ma-' Adjectives
grammarTopics.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root to describe plural nouns.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Mababait ang mga kapitbahay namin.
grammarTopics.english: Our neighbors are kind.

grammarTopics.title: Exclamatory 'Ang' + Adjective Root
grammarTopics.explanation: Drop 'ma-' and put 'ang' before the root to exclaim 'How [adjective]!'
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ang sarap nito! / Ang mahal naman!
grammarTopics.english: How delicious this is! / How expensive!

grammarTopics.title: Superlative 'Pinaka-'
grammarTopics.explanation: Attach 'pinaka-' to the full adjective to mean 'the most [adjective]'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ito ang pinakamasarap na halo-halo sa bayan.
grammarTopics.english: This is the most delicious halo-halo in town.

grammarTopics.title: Comparative 'Mas ... Kaysa Sa'
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'mas' before the adjective and 'kaysa sa' (than) to compare two things.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Mas malamig sa Tagaytay kaysa sa Maynila.
grammarTopics.english: It is colder in Tagaytay than in Manila.

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Ano' (What) & 'Anu-ano'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Ano' asks 'what' (singular); reduplicated 'anu-ano' asks 'what things' (plural).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Anong oras na? / Anu-ano ang bibilhin natin?
grammarTopics.english: What time is it? / What are the things we will buy?

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Sino' (Who) & 'Sinu-sino'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Sino' asks 'who'; 'sinu-sino' asks 'who all' (plural).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Sino ang kasama mo? / Sinu-sino ang pupunta?
grammarTopics.english: Who is with you? / Who all are going?

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Saan' vs. 'Nasaan' (Where)
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'saan' for where an action happens/goes; use 'nasaan' to ask the static location of a person/thing.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Saan ka pupunta? vs. Nasaan ang susi ko?
grammarTopics.english: Where are you going? vs. Where is my key?

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Kailan' (When)
grammarTopics.explanation: Asks about dates, days, or future/past times.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Kailan ang sahod? / Kailan ka uuwi ng probinsya?
grammarTopics.english: When is payday? / When are you going home to the province?

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Bakit' (Why) & 'Kasi / Dahil'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Bakit' asks 'why'; answer with 'kasi' (conversational) or 'dahil' (formal/written).
grammarTopics.tagalog: Bakit ka nagmamadali? — Kasi mahuhuli na ako sa klase.
grammarTopics.english: Why are you rushing? — Because I'm going to be late for class.

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Paano' (How)
grammarTopics.explanation: Asks for the manner or method of doing something.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Paano pumunta sa SM Megamall mula dito?
grammarTopics.english: How do I get to SM Megamall from here?

grammarTopics.title: Interrogative 'Magkano' vs. 'Ilan'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Magkano' asks 'how much (price)'; 'ilan' asks 'how many (count)'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Magkano isang kilo? / Ilan kayong sasakay?
grammarTopics.english: How much is one kilo? / How many of you are riding?

grammarTopics.title: Native Tagalog Numbers (Isa, Dalawa, Tatlo...)
grammarTopics.explanation: Used for counting objects, people, and general quantities (with linker '-ng' / 'na').
grammarTopics.tagalog: Dalawang order ng lugaw at tatlong tokwa.
grammarTopics.english: Two orders of congee and three fried tofu.

grammarTopics.title: Spanish-Derived Numbers for Money & Time
grammarTopics.explanation: Filipinos use Spanish-derived numbers (bente, singkwenta, alas-tres) for prices and clock time.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Singkwenta pesos lang. / Alas-sais na ng gabi.
grammarTopics.english: Fifty pesos only. / It's already 6:00 in the evening.

grammarTopics.title: Telling Time with 'Alas-' and 'Y Media'
grammarTopics.explanation: Prefix 'alas-' before hours (except 'ala-una' for 1:00) and 'y media' for :30.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Ala-una y media ng hapon.
grammarTopics.english: 1:30 in the afternoon.

grammarTopics.title: Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)
grammarTopics.explanation: Used with 'ng' for recurring times or 'sa' for upcoming times.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Magandang umaga po! / Kita tayo mamayang gabi.
grammarTopics.english: Good morning! / See you tonight.

grammarTopics.title: Past Time Marker 'Noong' / 'Nung'
grammarTopics.explanation: Marks completed past dates, days, or events ('last...' or 'when...').
grammarTopics.tagalog: Nung Linggo, nagsimba kami sa Quiapo.
grammarTopics.english: Last Sunday, we attended Mass in Quiapo.

grammarTopics.title: Future Time Marker 'Sa' + Day/Month
grammarTopics.explanation: Use 'sa' before days of the week or months to mean 'on/this coming...'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Sa Sabado ang outing ng barkada.
grammarTopics.english: The barkada's outing is on Saturday.

grammarTopics.title: Saying 'Before' ('Bago') and 'After' ('Pagkatapos')
grammarTopics.explanation: Connects sequential events in daily routines.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Maghugas ng kamay bago kumain.
grammarTopics.english: Wash your hands before eating.

grammarTopics.title: Conditional 'Kung' vs. 'Kapag' (Pag)
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Kung' is for uncertain 'if'; 'kapag' (colloquial 'pag') is for 'when/whenever' something happens.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Text mo ako pag nakauwi ka na.
grammarTopics.english: Text me when you get home.

grammarTopics.title: Expressing 'Even Though' ('Kahit')
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Kahit' means 'even if' or 'although'.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Pumasok siya sa trabaho kahit umuulan.
grammarTopics.english: He/She went to work even though it was raining.

grammarTopics.title: Expressing 'Instead of' ('Imbes Na')
grammarTopics.explanation: Shows choosing one option over another.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Naglakad na lang ako imbes na mag-tricycle.
grammarTopics.english: I just walked instead of taking a tricycle.

grammarTopics.title: Expressing 'Almost' ('Muntik Nang')
grammarTopics.explanation: Used for close calls in daily commuting or chores.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Muntik na akong maiwan ng bus!
grammarTopics.english: I almost missed the bus!

grammarTopics.title: Expressing 'It Depends' ('Depende Sa')
grammarTopics.explanation: A daily staple phrase when negotiating plans, prices, or traffic.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Depende kung hindi traffic sa C5.
grammarTopics.english: It depends if there's no traffic on C5.

grammarTopics.title: Softening Statements with 'Parang' and 'Medyo'
grammarTopics.explanation: 'Parang' (it seems/kind of) and 'medyo' (somewhat/a bit) keep Filipino speech indirect and polite.
grammarTopics.tagalog: Medyo malayo pa. / Parang uulan mamaya.
grammarTopics.english: It's still a bit far. / It looks like it might rain later.

scenarios.title: Passing the Jeepney Fare (Bayad Po)
scenarios.context: Sitting in the middle of a crowded jeepney and asking fellow passengers to pass your fare to the driver.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Bayad po, makikisuyo lang. Isa pong estudyante, galing Crossing.
Driver: Salamat! Sukli ng bente, isa galing Crossing!

scenarios.title: Stopping the Jeepney (Para Po)
scenarios.context: Signaling the jeepney driver to pull over safely at an unloading zone.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Para po sa tabi! Sa may tapat lang po ng Mercury Drug.
Driver: Sige, tabi lang tayo!

scenarios.title: Negotiating a Tricycle 'Special' Trip
scenarios.context: Asking a TODA tricycle driver for a solo ride straight to your street instead of waiting for other passengers.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Kuya, magkano pag special hanggang Phase 3? Nagmamadali na kasi ako.
Driver: Singkwenta pesos na lang, Ma'am. Sakay na po.

scenarios.title: MRT/LRT Beep Card Ticket Machine Issue
scenarios.context: Reporting to the station teller that the reload kiosk swallowed your bill without adding credit.
scenarios.dialogue:
Commuter: Ate, kinain po ng machine yung 100 pesos ko pero hindi nag-reflect sa Beep card.
Teller: Anong machine number po? Fill-upan niyo lang po itong incident slip.

scenarios.title: MRT/LRT Priority Lane & Skip Train
scenarios.context: Asking the platform guard where the priority queue is and if a skip train is arriving.
scenarios.dialogue:
Commuter: Kuya Guard, dito po ba yung pila para sa senior at buntis?
Guard: Opo, dito po sa harap. Hintayin natin yung parating na tren.

scenarios.title: Messaging Grab/Angkas Rider During Heavy Rain
scenarios.context: Reassuring your rider in the app chat so they don't cancel during payday rush hour rain.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Kuya, wag niyo po i-cancel, dagdagan ko na lang po sa tip, stranded po kami.
Rider: Sige po Ma'am, papunta na po ako, medyo traffic lang sa kanto.

scenarios.title: Guiding an Angkas/JoyRide Rider Through Inner Streets
scenarios.context: Giving turn-by-turn directions using familiar barangay landmarks.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Kuya, kanan po sa may kulay berdeng gate, tapat po ng bakery.
Rider: Copy po, dito na po ba sa tapat ng tindahan?

scenarios.title: Modern E-Jeepney Tap-In
scenarios.context: Asking the conductor about the fare and where to tap your card on an air-conditioned minibus.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Kuya, magkano po hanggang Cubao at saan po ita-tap itong card?
Conductor: Kinse pesos po. Dito lang po sa scanner pagbaba niyo.

scenarios.title: Provincial Bus Terminal (PITX / Cubao)
scenarios.context: Asking the dispatcher which gate the bus to Baguio or Batangas is parked at.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Boss, anong gate po yung bus pa-Baguio? Pwede pa po ba walk-in?
Dispatcher: Sa Gate 4, Boss. May bakante pa sa likod, akyat ka na.

scenarios.title: UV Express Seating Squeeze
scenarios.context: Politely telling the barker that the middle bench is already at full capacity.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Kuya, masikip na po, tatlo lang po talaga kasya dito sa gitna.
Barker: Sige, sa likod na lang yung isa. Larga na!

scenarios.title: Pedicab Ride Across a Flooded Street
scenarios.context: Negotiating with a pedicab driver to cross ankle-deep floodwater during monsoon rain.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Kuya, magkano patawid lang sa kabilang kanto? Baha na kasi masyado.
Driver: Bente pesos isa, Ma'am. Itaas niyo lang po yung paa niyo.

scenarios.title: RFID Balance Delay at NLEX/SLEX Tollgate
scenarios.context: Explaining to the toll teller that you just reloaded your Autosweep/Easytrip via GCash.
scenarios.dialogue:
Driver: Ma'am, kakapag-load ko lang po sa GCash limang minuto ang nakalipas.
Teller: Sige po Sir, patingin na lang po ng reference number para ma-manual encode natin.

scenarios.title: Flat Tire at a Roadside Vulcanizing Shop
scenarios.context: Asking the mechanic how long it will take to patch a punctured tire.
scenarios.dialogue:
Motorist: Boss, na-flat yung gulong ko sa likod. Gaano katagal po i-vulcanize?
Mechanic: Mga kinse minutos lang, Boss. Upo muna kayo.

scenarios.title: Subdivision Gate Visitor ID Check
scenarios.context: Leaving your valid ID at the HOA guardhouse when visiting a relative.
scenarios.dialogue:
Visitor: Good morning po, Guard. Bibisita lang po kay Tita Elena sa Phase 2, Block 5.
Guard: Paki-iwan na lang po ng isang valid ID at pakisulat ng pangalan sa logbook.

scenarios.title: Asking Locals for Directions (Pagtatanong)
scenarios.context: Asking bystanders at a street corner how to reach the municipal hall.
scenarios.dialogue:
Traveler: Magandang umaga po, saan po banda yung munisipyo dito? Nilalakad lang po ba?
Local: Diretsuhin mo lang itong kalsada, tapos kaliwa ka sa may simbahan.

scenarios.title: Paying Terminal Fees at a Ferry Port
scenarios.context: Asking port staff where to pay terminal and environmental fees before boarding a RoRo.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Miss, saan po nagbabayad ng terminal fee bago pumasok sa boarding gate?
Staff: Sa Window 2 po, Sir. Ipakita niyo lang po yung ticket niyo.

scenarios.title: NAIA Terminal Transfer Shuttle
scenarios.context: Asking airport staff how to transfer from NAIA Terminal 3 to Terminal 1.
scenarios.dialogue:
Traveler: Excuse me po, saan po yung sakayan ng shuttle papuntang Terminal 1?
Staff: Sa Arrival Bay 12 po, Ma'am. Every 30 minutes po ang alis.

scenarios.title: Reminding the Jeepney Driver About Change
scenarios.context: Politely reminding the driver of your change before getting off.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Manong, yung sukli ko po sa bente, isa lang po yung binayad ko.
Driver: Ay oo nga, pasensya na! Ito yung sukli mo.

scenarios.title: Checking Last Trip Schedule at Night
scenarios.context: Asking the jeepney barker if there are still trips heading to your area late at night.
scenarios.dialogue:
Commuter: Kuya, may biyahe pa po ba pa-Fairview?
Barker: Last trip na ito, Boss! Sakay na, aalis na rin kami.

scenarios.title: Asking a Seatmate to Move Over (Usog Lang Po)
scenarios.context: Asking passengers on a jeepney bench to slide over slightly so you can sit.
scenarios.dialogue:
Passenger: Makiki-usog lang po nang konti, isa pa daw po sabi ni Manong.
Seatmate: Sige po, upo na kayo.

scenarios.title: Buying in Tingi at a Sari-Sari Store
scenarios.context: Knocking on the store's metal grill with a coin to buy single sachets and ice water.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Pabili po! Isang sachet ng shampoo, isang bawang, at dalawang ice tubig.
Store Owner: Sandali lang! Ito na, kinse pesos lahat.

scenarios.title: Deposito sa Bote (Empty Glass Bottle Promise)
scenarios.context: Promising to return the glass soda bottle after pouring the drink into a cup.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Ate, isalin ko lang po sa baso yung Coke, ibabalik ko rin po agad yung bote.
Store Owner: Sige, walang problema, basta balik mo agad ha.

scenarios.title: Haggling (Tawad) in Divisoria or Baclaran
scenarios.context: Asking for a discount or 'buena mano' price when buying multiple items.
scenarios.dialogue:
Shopper: Ate, magkano kung tatlo kukunin ko? Baka pwedeng bawasan pa, buena mano naman!
Vendor: Sige na nga, 250 na lang yung tatlo para sa'yo.

scenarios.title: Buying Fresh Fish at the Wet Market (Palengke)
scenarios.context: Checking the freshness of fish and asking the vendor to scale and clean it.
scenarios.dialogue:
Shopper: Sariwa po ba itong galunggong? Isang kilo nga po, paki-kaliskisan at paki-linis na rin.
Vendor: Bagong huli lang yan, Ma'am! Hintayin niyo lang saglit, lilinisin ko na.

scenarios.title: Asking for Dagdag (Freebie) on Fruits
scenarios.context: Playfully asking the vendor for one extra piece after weighing a kilo of mangoes or calamansi.
scenarios.dialogue:
Shopper: Ate, sakto na sa isang kilo. Baka may pa-dagdag ka naman diyang isang piraso!
Vendor: O sige, dagdagan natin ng isa para bumalik ka ulit!

scenarios.title: Paying with a 1,000-Peso Bill Early in the Morning
scenarios.context: Apologizing for not having smaller bills and offering to pay via GCash.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Pasensya na po, wala pa akong barya sa isang libo. Pwede po ba mag-GCash na lang?
Cashier: Opo Ma'am, pwede po. I-scan niyo na lang po yung QR code dito.

scenarios.title: GCash Cash-In at the Neighborhood Store
scenarios.context: Handing over cash and your mobile number for a GCash cash-in transaction.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Ate, pa-cash in po ng 500. Ito po yung number ko, may 10 pesos na po diyan para sa fee.
Store Owner: Paki-check kung tama yung pangalan na lumabas sa screen.

scenarios.title: Buying Hot Pandesal at 6:00 AM
scenarios.context: Asking the local bakery if the pandesal is freshly baked from the oven.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Kuya, mainit pa po ba yung pandesal? Pabili pong trenta pesos at isang Reno.
Baker: Kakalabas lang sa pugon niyan, Ate! Mainit-init pa.

scenarios.title: Catching the Morning Taho Vendor
scenarios.context: Calling out to the taho vendor with your own mug for extra sago and arnibal.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Manong, taho! Sandali lang po, kukuha lang ako ng baso. Pa-dagdag po ng sago!
Vendor: Sige po, bente pesos po itong malaking baso.

scenarios.title: Ordering Turo-Turo at a Carinderia
scenarios.context: Pointing at viands and asking for complimentary sinigang broth.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Ate, kalahating gulay, isang pork chop, at pahingi po ng sabaw na may sinigang.
Server: Dito niyo po kakainin o take-out?

scenarios.title: Buying Street Food (Tusok-Tusok)
scenarios.context: Standing by the fishball cart and asking which jar has spicy vinegar.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Kuya, alin po dito yung maanghang na suka? Dalawang order nga po ng kwek-kwek.
Vendor: Yung may sili sa kanan, Boss. Wag mo lang isasawsaw yung nakagatan na ha!

scenarios.title: Ordering Halo-Halo in April
scenarios.context: Customizing your halo-halo toppings at a summer stand.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Ate, isang special halo-halo nga po, pa-extra ng leche flan pero wag na po lagyan ng kaong.
Vendor: Sige po, hintayin niyo lang saglit, ikakaskas ko na yung yelo.

scenarios.title: Water Refilling Station Delivery
scenarios.context: Texting or calling your local water station to deliver purified water gallons.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Kuya, pa-deliver po ng tatlong slim at isang bilog na galon, dito po sa dulo.
Delivery Rider: Sige po Ma'am, i-schedule ko na po ngayong hapon.

scenarios.title: Ordering an LPG Tank Replacement
scenarios.context: Calling the gas dealer because the stove ran out of gas mid-cooking.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Hello, pa-deliver po ng isang 11kg LPG tank sa Block 4 Lot 12, naubusan po kami habang nagluluto.
Staff: On the way na po yung rider namin, mga sampung minuto lang.

scenarios.title: Mall Entrance Bag Inspection
scenarios.context: Opening your backpack for the security guard at the mall entrance.
scenarios.dialogue:
Shopper: Good morning po, Guard. Ito po yung bag ko.
Guard: Salamat po, Ma'am. Enjoy shopping!

scenarios.title: Asking for Sizes at a Department Store
scenarios.context: Asking the sales attendant to check the stockroom for a medium size.
scenarios.dialogue:
Shopper: Miss, may Medium pa po kayo nito sa stockroom, o last piece na po ito sa rack?
Attendant: Check ko lang po saglit sa stockroom, Sir. Ano pong kulay?

scenarios.title: Supermarket Senior Citizen / PWD Priority Lane
scenarios.context: Presenting your grandmother's OSCA ID and booklet at the checkout counter.
scenarios.dialogue:
Shopper: Miss, ito po yung Senior Citizen ID at booklet ng lola ko para sa discount.
Cashier: Sige po, paki-pirma na lang po dito sa booklet pagkatapos ma-punch.

scenarios.title: Asking for Unli-Rice Refill at Mang Inasal
scenarios.context: Catching the server's attention during peak lunch hour for extra rice and soup.
scenarios.dialogue:
Diner: Kuya, pa-refill naman po ng extra rice at sabaw pagdaan niyo!
Server: Sige po Sir, kuha lang po ako ng mainit na kanin.

scenarios.title: Ordering Samgyupsal Refills
scenarios.context: Asking the restaurant staff for another round of pork belly and lettuce.
scenarios.dialogue:
Diner: Ate, pa-refill po ng dalawang samgyupsal plain, lettuce, at cheese!
Server: Copy po, i-serve po namin agad.

scenarios.title: Splitting the Bill (KKB - Kanya-Kanyang Bayad)
scenarios.context: Calculating everyone's share after eating out with friends.
scenarios.dialogue:
Friend 1: Magkano ambag natin isa? I-send ko na lang sa GCash mo.
Friend 2: 285 pesos each! Na-send ko na sa GC yung QR code ko.

scenarios.title: Receiving a Shopee/Lazada COD Parcel
scenarios.context: Answering the delivery rider's morning call and confirming exact cash.
scenarios.dialogue:
Rider: Ma'am, Shopee po, nandito na po sa labas ng gate, 349 pesos po.
Buyer: Opo Kuya, bababa na po ako, sakto na po yung bayad.

scenarios.title: Leaving COD Cash with a Neighbor
scenarios.context: Asking your trusted neighbor to receive and pay for your parcel while you are at work.
scenarios.dialogue:
Neighbor 1: Ate Marites, makikisuyo po sana, iiwan ko po yung 350 pesos para sa Shopee parcel ko.
Neighbor 2: Sige, iwan mo lang dito sa mesa, ako na mag-aabot pag dumating.

scenarios.title: Submitting an Unboxing Video for Refund
scenarios.context: Messaging an online seller with your uncut unboxing video to request a refund.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Hello seller, basag po yung item pagbukas ko. I-attach ko po yung full unboxing video.
Seller: Pasensya na po, paki-file na lang po ng Return/Refund sa app para ma-approve namin.

scenarios.title: Delayed GCash OTP Inside a Mall
scenarios.context: Explaining to the cashier why your mobile payment confirmation is taking a moment.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Sandali lang po Miss, mahina po kasi signal dito sa loob, hinihintay ko lang yung OTP.
Cashier: Walang problema po, Ma'am. Patingin na lang po ng receipt pag pumasok na.

scenarios.title: Reporting Blinking Red LOS Internet Outage
scenarios.context: Calling your internet provider (PLDT/Converge/Globe) when the modem shows a red LOS light.
scenarios.dialogue:
Subscriber: Good morning, blinking red po yung LOS light ng modem namin simula kagabi pa.
Agent: Check ko po yung line status niyo. May reported area outage po sa barangay niyo.

scenarios.title: Asking a Friend for Mobile Hotspot
scenarios.context: Borrowing a quick hotspot connection so you can register a data promo.
scenarios.dialogue:
Friend 1: Pre, pa-hotspot saglit, maglo-load lang ako sa GlobeOne app.
Friend 2: Sige, naka-on na, 'AndroidAP' yung pangalan.

scenarios.title: Facebook Marketplace Meet-Up vs. Lalamove
scenarios.context: Coordinating with a seller whether to meet at an MRT station or book a courier.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Boss, pwede ba meet-up sa MRT Shaw turnstile mamayang 6 PM?
Seller: Medyo malayo ako doon, Boss. Pa-Lalamove mo na lang, hati tayo sa delivery fee.

scenarios.title: Instructing a Lalamove Courier
scenarios.context: Confirming the pinned address and who pays the delivery fee.
scenarios.dialogue:
Sender: Kuya, naka-pin na po yung exact address. Sender na lang po magbabayad ng fee.
Rider: Sige po Ma'am, nandito na po ako sa pickup point.

scenarios.title: Warning Parents About Text Phishing Scams
scenarios.context: Alerting your parents in the family group chat not to click suspicious links.
scenarios.dialogue:
Child: Ma, Pa, wag niyo po iki-click yung text na may link tungkol sa points o raffle, scam po yan.
Parent: Buti sinabi mo anak, ide-delete ko na agad.

scenarios.title: Using a Neighborhood Piso Wi-Fi Vendo
scenarios.context: Dropping coins into a Piso Wi-Fi machine to finish submitting schoolwork.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Ate, maghuhulog lang po ako ng sampung piso sa Piso Wi-Fi niyo.
Owner: Sige lang, pindutin mo lang yung 'Insert Coin' sa portal.

scenarios.title: Paying Bills via 7-Eleven CLiQQ Kiosk
scenarios.context: Asking the clerk for help when the CLiQQ receipt printer runs out of paper.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Kuya, naubusan po ng papel yung CLiQQ machine, magbabayad po sana ako ng Meralco.
Clerk: Ay sandali lang po Sir, palitan ko lang po yung thermal paper.

scenarios.title: InstaPay vs. PESONet Bank Transfer
scenarios.context: Reassuring a client that you sent payment via InstaPay for instant crediting.
scenarios.dialogue:
Client: Na-transfer ko na po via InstaPay para mag-reflect agad sa account niyo today.
Merchant: Confirmed po! Na-receive na namin, ipapadala na namin yung order niyo.

scenarios.title: Foodpanda / GrabFood Condo Lobby Drop-Off
scenarios.context: Giving instructions to your food delivery rider for condo concierge drop-off.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Kuya, paki-iwan na lang po sa lobby concierge table, no need for plastic utensils.
Rider: Sige po Ma'am, na-iwan ko na po kay Kuya Guard.

scenarios.title: Asking for Wi-Fi Password at a Coffee Shop
scenarios.context: Asking the barista for the Wi-Fi voucher code after ordering.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Miss, ano pong Wi-Fi password niyo dito?
Barista: Nasa ilalim po ng official receipt niyo yung Wi-Fi code, Sir.

scenarios.title: Topping Up Load at a Convenience Store
scenarios.context: Buying regular load or an e-PIN at the counter.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Kuya, pa-load po ng 100 sa Smart.
Clerk: Pakisulat na lang po yung mobile number niyo dito sa notepad.

scenarios.title: Pagmamano at a Family Gathering
scenarios.context: Greeting elders upon arriving at a family reunion or Sunday visit.
scenarios.dialogue:
Visitor: Magandang tanghali po, Lolo, Lola. Mano po.
Grandparent: Kaawaan ka ng Diyos, apo. Kumain na ba kayo?

scenarios.title: Bringing Home Pasalubong
scenarios.context: Handing over snacks or local delicacies after coming home from work or a trip.
scenarios.dialogue:
Worker: Ma, may dala akong pasalubong na buko pie at ensaymada sa kusina.
Mother: Naku, nag-abala ka pa! Timpla tayo ng kape.

scenarios.title: Packing 'Sharon' (Take-Home Food) at a Fiesta
scenarios.context: Being urged by the host to pack leftover party food to bring home.
scenarios.dialogue:
Host: O, mag-balot ka na ng menudo at shanghai para sa mga bata sa bahay!
Guest: Naku Tita, salamat po! Magbabalot na po ako ng konti.

scenarios.title: The 'Last Piece' Etiquette (Hiya)
scenarios.context: Asking everyone at the table before taking the final piece of food on a shared platter.
scenarios.dialogue:
Diner 1: Sino pa kakain nitong huling piraso ng lumpia?
Diner 2: Sige, kunin mo na, busog na ako!

scenarios.title: Inviting a Passerby to Eat ('Kain tayo!')
scenarios.context: Offering food to a neighbor or coworker who walks past while you are eating.
scenarios.dialogue:
Person Eating: Kain po tayo! Mainit pa yung sinigang.
Passerby: Sige lang, salamat! Katatapos lang din naming mag-tanghalian.

scenarios.title: Checking During a Sudden Brownout
scenarios.context: Asking your neighbor over the fence if the power outage affects the whole street.
scenarios.dialogue:
Neighbor 1: Mare, brownout din ba sa inyo o sa amin lang nag-trip yung breaker?
Neighbor 2: Wala rin dito sa amin! Nag-post na daw ang Meralco sa Facebook.

scenarios.title: Preparing for a Typhoon (Signal #3)
scenarios.context: Coordinating with family members to store water and charge power banks before a storm.
scenarios.dialogue:
Parent: I-charge niyo na lahat ng power bank at punuin na yung mga drum ng tubig.
Child: Opo, nakahanda na rin yung flashlight at emergency radio.

scenarios.title: Floodwater Entering the Garage
scenarios.context: Moving appliances and shoes to higher ground during heavy monsoon rain.
scenarios.dialogue:
Family Member 1: Iakyat na natin yung electric fan at mga sapatos sa second floor!
Family Member 2: Sige, kunin ko na rin yung extension cord sa baba.

scenarios.title: Borrowing a Ladder from Next Door
scenarios.context: Asking a neighbor over the gate if you can borrow a ladder briefly.
scenarios.dialogue:
Neighbor 1: Kuya Bert, pwede po ba makahiram ng hagdan saglit? Magpapalit lang po ako ng bumbilya.
Neighbor 2: Sige, kunin mo lang doon sa may garahe namin.

scenarios.title: 10:00 PM Karaoke Curfew Reminder
scenarios.context: Politely asking a neighbor to lower the videoke volume late at night.
scenarios.dialogue:
Neighbor: Pasensya na po, baka pwedeng pahinaan na lang po nang konti yung videoke, may pasok pa kami bukas.
Host: Ay pasensya na po! Hihinaan na po namin agad.

scenarios.title: Sunday Family Lunch After Mass
scenarios.context: Deciding as a family after Sunday morning Mass where to eat lunch.
scenarios.dialogue:
Parent: Saan tayo magta-tanghalian pagkatapos ng Misa?
Child: Mag-Mang Inasal na lang tayo, Pa, para may unli-rice!

scenarios.title: Rescuing Laundry (Sampayan) From Sudden Rain
scenarios.context: Calling everyone at home to pull dry clothes off the clothesline when rain starts.
scenarios.dialogue:
Parent: Umuulan na! Tulungan niyo akong hanguin yung mga sinampay sa labas!
Child: Nandiyan na po, kukunin ko na yung mga tuwalya!

scenarios.title: OFW Balikbayan Box Video Call
scenarios.context: Talking to an aunt abroad on Messenger while she packs a balikbayan box.
scenarios.dialogue:
Niece: Tita, wag niyo na po masyadong damihan yung chocolates, baka mag-overweight yung box!
Aunt: Hindi yan, sakto lang sa sukat ng LBC box.

scenarios.title: Claiming Remittance at Palawan / Cebuana
scenarios.context: Presenting your control number and valid ID at the remittance counter.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Miss, magki-claim po ng padala. Ito po yung control number at yung valid ID ko.
Teller: Paki-fill out lang po itong receive form at paki-pirma sa ibaba.

scenarios.title: Hiring an Aircon Cleaning Technician
scenarios.context: Explaining an issue with your window-type AC and asking for the service rate.
scenarios.dialogue:
Homeowner: Kuya, maingay na po yung aircon namin at hindi na masyadong malamig. Magkano general cleaning?
Technician: 600 pesos po pag window-type, Ma'am.

scenarios.title: Rushing Out for the Garbage Truck
scenarios.context: Bringing out segregated trash bags when the barangay garbage truck sounds its horn.
scenarios.dialogue:
Resident: Kuya, sandali lang po! Ito na po yung nabubulok at di-nabubulok.
Collector: Sige po, iabot niyo na lang dito.

scenarios.title: Securing Trash Bins from Stray Animals
scenarios.context: Discussing with family how to keep stray cats and dogs from scattering garbage.
scenarios.dialogue:
Parent: Lagyan natin ng tali yung takip ng basurahan para hindi mahalungkat ng mga pusa sa gabi.
Child: Sige Pa, itatali ko na po.

scenarios.title: Welcoming a Guest ('Tuloy Po Kayo')
scenarios.context: Inviting a visitor inside the house and offering water or snacks.
scenarios.dialogue:
Host: Uy, nandiyan ka na pala! Tuloy po kayo, upo muna kayo. Gusto mo ba ng juice o kape?
Guest: Salamat! Tubig na lang muna, medyo mainit sa labas.

scenarios.title: Joining a Neighborhood Paluwagan
scenarios.context: Checking with the organizer which payout slot is still available.
scenarios.dialogue:
Member: Ate, anong petsa pa po yung bakanteng sahod sa paluwagan niyo ngayong cut-off?
Organizer: Yung katapusan ng buwan na lang ang bakante, kunin mo na ba?

scenarios.title: The 'Filipino Goodbye' at the Gate
scenarios.context: Saying goodbye inside the house, then continuing to chat for 20 minutes by the gate.
scenarios.dialogue:
Guest: Una na po kami, Tita! Ingat po kayo dito... ay oo nga pala, tungkol dun sa sinabi mo kanina...
Host: Sige, ingat din kayo! Chat mo ako pag nakauwi na kayo.

scenarios.title: Waiting for #WalangPasok Announcements
scenarios.context: Checking the Mayor's official page at 5:30 AM during a storm while getting ready for school.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student 1: Naka-uniform na ako, nag-announce na ba si Mayor kung walang pasok?
Student 2: Kakapost lang! Suspended na all levels!

scenarios.title: Asking a Professor for a Deadline Extension
scenarios.context: Messaging your instructor politely when a power outage interrupts your online submission.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Good evening po, Sir. Nag-brownout po sa area namin kaya na-delay yung upload ko sa Canvas.
Professor: Noted, just submit it as soon as your power is restored.

scenarios.title: Reminding a Groupmate in Thesis
scenarios.context: Following up with a group member in the Messenger GC to finish their assigned chapter.
scenarios.dialogue:
Leader: Guys, bukas na yung defense draft. Yung part mo sa Chapter 2 na lang yung kulang.
Member: Pasensya na, tinatapos ko na yung RRL ngayon, i-upload ko before 10 PM.

scenarios.title: Rush Printing (Pa-Print Po) Outside Campus
scenarios.context: Asking the computer shop attendant to print your paper right before class starts.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Kuya, pa-print po, short bond paper, black and white lang. Rush po, malelate na ako!
Attendant: Send mo na sa Messenger o email namin para ma-print agad.

scenarios.title: Asking a Seatmate for Yellow Pad Paper
scenarios.context: Whispering to a classmate during a surprise quiz to ask for a sheet of paper.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student 1: Pst, pahingi namang one-fourth o kaya one-whole yellow pad.
Student 2: O, hati na tayo dito sa isang piraso.

scenarios.title: University Teacher's Prerogative (Prerog)
scenarios.context: Asking a professor on the first day of classes if they can accept one more student.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Good morning po, Ma'am. Pwede pa po ba magpa-prerog sa class niyo?
Professor: Isulat mo lang yung student number mo sa class list sa harap.

scenarios.title: Signing of Semester Clearance
scenarios.context: Going to the library or office to get signatures for your exam permit.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Ma'am, magpapa-sign lang po sana ng clearance para makuha ko na yung exam permit ko.
Staff: Wala ka namang overdue books, pirmahan ko na.

scenarios.title: Ordering at the School Canteen During Recess
scenarios.context: Buying snacks quickly during a short 15-minute break.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Ate, isang banana cue at isang calamansi juice nga po, nag-bell na kasi.
Vendor: Ito na, bente-singko lahat.

scenarios.title: Asking Parents for Permission (Paalam)
scenarios.context: Asking your parents if you can go to a classmate's house on Saturday for a school project.
scenarios.dialogue:
Student: Ma, pwede po ba ako pumunta kina Bea sa Sabado? Magpa-practice lang po kami ng sayaw sa PE.
Parent: Sige, basta umuwi ka bago mag-alas sais ng gabi ha.

scenarios.title: Collecting Class Ambagan (Contribution)
scenarios.context: Collecting 50 pesos per student for a class event or teacher's gift.
scenarios.dialogue:
Treasurer: Guys, yung 50 pesos na ambagan para sa cake ni Ma'am, pakibigay na bago mag-uwian.
Classmate: Pwede bang GCash na lang? Wala akong barya eh.

scenarios.title: PRC Board Exam / CET Proctor Instructions
scenarios.context: Checking with the room proctor about required transparent envelopes and pencil rules.
scenarios.dialogue:
Examinee: Sir, pwede po ba ipasok yung transparent plastic envelope at Mongol #2 pencil sa upuan?
Proctor: Opo, iwan niyo lang po yung mga bag at cellphone dito sa harap.

scenarios.title: Requesting TOR and Good Moral Certificate
scenarios.context: Asking the registrar how many working days it takes to release graduation credentials.
scenarios.dialogue:
Graduate: Good morning po, ilang working days po bago ma-release yung Transcript of Records?
Registrar: Mga 7 to 10 working days po pagkatapos magbayad sa cashier.

scenarios.title: NBI Clearance 'With Hit' Status
scenarios.context: Checking with the NBI clerk when to return after getting a 'Hit' for a common surname.
scenarios.dialogue:
Applicant: Ma'am, may 'Hit' daw po yung pangalan ko. Anong petsa po ako babalik?
Clerk: Balik po kayo pagkatapos ng 8 working days, dalhin niyo lang po itong claim stub.

scenarios.title: LTO Driver's License Renewal
scenarios.context: Asking the LTO window clerk about the medical clinic and plastic card availability.
scenarios.dialogue:
Driver: Boss, saan po yung accredited medical clinic dito, at plastic card na po ba yung iri-release?
Clerk: Sa kabilang building po yung medical, at opo, may plastic card na tayo today.

scenarios.title: Updating Records at SSS, PhilHealth, or Pag-IBIG
scenarios.context: Verifying with the guard if your photocopied IDs and specimen signatures are complete.
scenarios.dialogue:
Member: Kuya Guard, kumpleto na po ba itong photocopy ng dalawang valid ID na may tatlong pirma?
Guard: Kumpleto na po, Ma'am. Kumuha na po kayo ng number sa Window 1.

scenarios.title: Getting a Barangay Clearance
scenarios.context: Requesting an official certificate at the barangay hall for job application.
scenarios.dialogue:
Resident: Magandang umaga po, kukuha po sana ako ng Barangay Clearance para sa job application ko.
Secretary: Pakipakita lang po ng valid ID o cedula para ma-type na natin.

scenarios.title: Filing a Sick Leave (SL) via Chat
scenarios.context: Notifying your supervisor early in the morning that you have a fever.
scenarios.dialogue:
Employee: Good morning TL, magfa-file po sana ako ng Sick Leave today dahil may lagnat ako.
Supervisor: Get well soon! Just send your teleconsult med cert once you're feeling better.

scenarios.title: BPO Graveyard Shift Coffee Break
scenarios.context: Ordering 2:00 AM iced coffee with teammates during your mid-shift break.
scenarios.dialogue:
Agent 1: Tara sa baba, mag-iced coffee muna tayo bago bumalik sa queue.
Agent 2: Game! Antok na antok na rin ako eh.

scenarios.title: Checking the ATM on Payday (15th/30th)
scenarios.context: Waiting in a long payday ATM line and hoping the machine still has cash.
scenarios.dialogue:
Worker 1: Sana hindi pa offline o ubos yung cash sa ATM, ang haba na ng pila.
Worker 2: Kakapag-reload lang daw ng armored van kanina, may laman pa yan!

scenarios.title: Organizing an Office Potluck
scenarios.context: Coordinating in the team chat who is bringing pancit, pichi-pichi, and drinks.
scenarios.dialogue:
Coworker 1: Guys, ako na bahala sa Amber's pancit malabon at pichi-pichi!
Coworker 2: Ako na sasagot sa soft drinks at yelo!

scenarios.title: Greeting Inaanak on Christmas Day
scenarios.context: Handing out crisp bills in red angpao envelopes to your godchildren.
scenarios.dialogue:
Godparent: Merry Christmas! Mag-aral nang mabuti ha, ito yung aguinaldo mo kay Ninong.
Child: Mano po, Ninong! Thank you po!

scenarios.title: Requesting an HMO LOA at the Hospital
scenarios.context: Asking the hospital HMO concierge for a Letter of Authorization before a check-up.
scenarios.dialogue:
Patient: Good morning po, magpapa-approve po sana ako ng LOA para sa consultation sa Internal Medicine.
Concierge: Paki-abot na lang po ng HMO card at valid ID niyo, Ma'am.

scenarios.title: Buying Generic Medicine at Mercury Drug
scenarios.context: Asking the pharmacist if a more affordable generic equivalent is available.
scenarios.dialogue:
Customer: Miss, meron po bang generic equivalent itong nireseta ng doktor?
Pharmacist: Opo Sir, meron po kaming RiteMED para dito.

scenarios.title: Making Sure a Barkada Outing Isn't 'Drawing'
scenarios.context: Collecting downpayments in the group chat for a Pansol or Elyu trip.
scenarios.dialogue:
Organizer: Guys, mag-send na kayo ng 500 downpayment para hindi na naman ito maging drawing!
Friend: Nag-send na ako sa GCash mo! Tuloy na tuloy na ito!

scenarios.title: Simbang Gabi and Hot Bibingka / Puto Bumbong
scenarios.context: Ordering traditional Christmas delicacies outside the church after dawn Mass.
scenarios.dialogue:
Buyer: Ate, dalawang puto bumbong at isang bibingka nga po, pa-dagdag po ng niyog at asukal.
Vendor: Sige po, mainit-init pa ito, bagong luto lang.
